question_text: Name one thing the U.S. Constitution does.
lead_in: You only need to name one — the Constitution does all of these:

official_answers.text: Protects the rights of the people

why_it_matters.text: In 1787, most countries ran on a king's word or unwritten custom. The Constitution did something new — it wrote the rules down. It builds the government (a Congress to make laws, a President to enforce them, courts to judge) and limits it too, by protecting people's rights.

fun_fact.text: Of every written national constitution on Earth, the U.S. Constitution is both the oldest still in use and one of the shortest — only about 4,500 words. The whole rulebook for the government is shorter than many a school essay.
